summary.headline: Jupiter Wagons FY26 PAT of INR166 crore on INR2,961 crore total income; Q4 PAT fell to INR27 crore amid wheelset and consumables disruptions.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated total income was INR2,961 crore, EBITDA INR363 crore (12.4% margin) and PAT INR166 crore. Q4 total income was INR790 crore, EBITDA INR83 crore and PAT INR27 crore, with management attributing the weakness to wheelset shortages in the first half and LPG-linked supply chain and consumables disruptions in Q4. Order book entering FY27 stands at INR4,675 crore, and the wheelset subsidiary crossed INR500 crore revenue at about 17% EBITDA margin. Management guided to wagon execution recovery from Q2 FY27 and a large Indian Railways wagon tender expected within two quarters, though no firm timelines were given.

financial_highlights.value: Above INR500 crore in FY26; INR528 crore per Q&A

segments.name: Wheelsets (Jupiter Tatravagonka Railwheel Factory)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from INR343 crore to INR528 crore with EBITDA margin about 17% vs 12% last year. Won 9,000 LHB axles order from Ministry of Railways and an LoI for 5,376 Vande Bharat wheelsets.

segments.name: Wagons (freight and private)
segments.commentary: Pending order book about 2,000 wagons for Indian Railways and about 5,400 non-Railway wagons, totalling about INR3,100 crore. Q4 private wagon execution was 1,347 units; execution was moderated to current levels pending new orders.

segments.name: Batteries / BESS (Jupiter Electric Mobility)
segments.commentary: MoAs with Chalukya Power and Pickrenew Energy add 110 MW of BESS to FY27 order book. Target of INR1,000 crore revenue in batteries and energy storage over 3 to 4 years; cell-to-battery line commissioned in Indore.

segments.name: Stone India (freight brake systems)
segments.commentary: Received RDSO approval for freight brake system; commercial production expected from July 2026, with management expecting profitability this year. Passenger brakes are handled via JV with Dako.

segments.name: Containers
segments.commentary: Healthy growth in FY26. Management expects container revenue to double in FY27, contingent on PLI scheme specifics; no subsidy percentage confirmed.

guidance_outlook: Odisha greenfield wheelset plant: interim/partial production by March 2027 and full commissioning by March 2028 (per Q&A; opening remarks said end of FY28 for full commissioning).
Wagon execution expected to recover from Q2 FY27; a substantial jump depends on Indian Railways order book release, expected within two quarters.
Container revenue expected to double in FY27, subject to PLI policy details.
Stone India expected to turn profitable in FY27.
Long-term target: about INR10,000 crore revenue and at least 15% EBITDA margin by 2030.
Entry into passenger rolling stock in FY27 via a strategic partnership (not yet named); 2-ton truck (JEM TEZ) 1 or 2 variants to launch in FY27.
capex_capacity: Odisha greenfield wheelset project: all critical equipment ordered, deliveries commenced, civil construction at advanced stage; interim operations delayed about two quarters due to shipping disruptions.
Stone India freight brake facility at Port Trust land; licensing completed, commercial production from July 2026.
Cell-to-battery manufacturing line commissioned in Indore; modular BESS in 10-ft and 20-ft container formats developed.
Wagon capacity not being expanded further until new order book arrives.
Container capacity focused on specialised containers; expansion to marine containers planned if PLI policy materialises.
demand_pricing: Indian Railways wagon tender expected this year; management expects it to cover at least three years of Railways requirements and expects a strong market share.
Management said Corten steel availability is not a constraint in India; the issue is pricing versus China, which the PLI is meant to bridge.
Management cited a 8% to 10% PLI subsidy range as its understanding, but said no official specifics have been released.
Management said it is not pursuing wagon leasing; it relies on its partnership with GATX for private leasing.
BESS demand expected to grow strongly as industrial and consumer users shift from gensets to lithium-ion; imports, especially from China, remain significant.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Odisha wheelset plant been delayed from Q2 FY27 to Q4 FY27, and what is the FY28 ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said final commissioning remains on schedule for FY28; only interim operations slipped about two quarters due to shipping disruptions. Interim now March 2027 and final March 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventories rise from INR769 crore to INR1,079 crore, and when will inventory days normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to unanticipated disruptions that broke production timelines; it expects stabilisation and more stability from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pending wagon order book and private wagon execution?
qa_highlights.answer: About 2,000 wagons for Indian Railways and about 5,400 non-Railway wagons, totalling about INR3,100 crore; Q4 private wagon execution was 1,347 units.

qa_highlights.question: How will Jupiter qualify for passenger rolling stock, and what scope and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Lacking prior passenger rolling stock experience, it is finalising a strategic tie-up with a global rolling stock maker; scope, capex and structure (JV or in-house) not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are subsidiary EBITDA margins lower in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Railwheel margin improved to 17%; the drag came from Stone India (one-time Port Trust licence renewal fee last year, capex) and JEM expansion costs, which should improve this year.

qa_highlights.question: Will Jupiter's wagon execution recover, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-Railway execution will pick up as disruptions ease, with recovery from Q2 FY27; execution was held back to avoid capacity expansion ahead of new orders.

risks_watch: Repeated delays: Odisha interim operations slipped about two quarters; further shipping or supply-chain slippage would push commissioning.
Indian Railways wagon tender timing is uncertain; management gave no firm date beyond 'within two quarters'.
Working capital: inventory rose about 40% to INR1,079 crore; normalisation relies on Q2 FY27 stability.
PLI container scheme terms remain unannounced; the expected container doubling depends on it.
Passenger rolling stock entry depends on an unnamed partner; structure and capex undisclosed.
Q4 PAT of INR27 crore vs FY26 PAT of INR166 crore indicates weak run-rate; the TEZ monthly run rate was not disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and the rail policy backdrop, but cautious and often non-specific on near-term timing: several answers deferred details (tender size, passenger partner, PLI specifics, TEZ volumes) to later disclosure.
key_quotes: So definitely, we expect the numbers to be much better than the previous financial year.
We enter FY27 with an order book of INR4,675 crore, providing healthy revenue visibility and reaffirming customer confidence in our capabilities and execution.
Our aim is to focus on our core competence, which is wagon manufacturing and the leasing part for the time being, it should be taken care by the experts.
we are very, very bullish on the sector, and we have a very, very long-term view on the sector.

growth.why: Management guides to wagon execution recovery from Q2 FY27 and container revenue doubling in FY27, backed by a INR4,675 crore order book, 9,000 LHB axle order and 110 MW BESS MoAs, but wagon recovery depends on an unreleased Railways tender with no firm timeline and the Odisha interim start slipped to March 2027.
